chapterTitle: चार अक्षर वाले शब्दों का अभ्यास
pages:
• **Introduction to DAV Class UKG Bal Madhuri Chapter 5**: Welcome to the comprehensive academic study notes for Chapter 5 titled "चार अक्षर वाले शब्दों का अभ्यास" (Practice of Four-Letter Words) published under the Dayanand Anglo-Vedic Public School Board curriculum.
• **Core Linguistic Objective**: The primary educational goal of this chapter is to transition young learners from three-letter words (तीन अक्षर वाले शब्द) to four-letter non-compound words (चार अक्षर वाले शब्द) without the use of matras (अमात्रिक शब्द).
• **Foundational Reading Skill**: Students learn the essential phonetic synthesis mechanism of blending four distinct consonant sounds sequentially to form meaningful Hindi vocabulary words.
• **Visual-Aural Association**: The chapter employs brightly colored illustrations alongside simple four-letter words to facilitate picture-word association and reinforce vocabulary retention among UKG students.
• **Phonetic Building Blocks**: Each four-letter word is treated as an assembly of four individual consonant phonemes (वर्ण), demonstrating how building blocks of the Hindi alphabet combine without vowel modifications.
• **Prerequisite Knowledge Review**: Mastery of this chapter requires prior recognition and fluent reading of all base consonants (व्यंजन) from 'क' (ka) to 'ज्ञ' (gya) as taught in earlier DAV curriculum modules.
• **Absence of Matras**: A core pedagogical rule emphasized throughout the chapter is that none of the four-letter words contain any dependent vowel signs (मात्राएँ), keeping the spelling purely phonetic and direct.
• **Syllabic Rhythm Development**: Students are trained to read these words by breaking them down into two halves—the first two letters and the last two letters—to maintain a natural reading cadence.
• **Cognitive Load Management**: The DAV curriculum strategically introduces four-letter words only after students have gained complete confidence in recognizing and writing two-letter and three-letter words.
• **Vocabulary Selection Criteria**: Words chosen in Chapter 5 are restricted to familiar, everyday objects, common actions, and simple nouns that are easily understood by a four-to-five-year-old child.
• **Writing Alignment Practice**: The chapter serves as a bridge for fine-motor skill development, encouraging children to write longer continuous letter clusters under a straight headline (सिरोरेखा).
• **Role of the Teacher/Parent**: Educators and parents are guided to use phonetic sounding (ध्वनि उच्चारण) rather than rote spelling memorization when introducing these longer lexical units.
• **Sequential Progression**: The chapter begins with the simplest combinations of four consonants and gradually introduces more complex sounding words as the student progresses through the pages.
• **Classroom Interaction Strategy**: Collaborative reading aloud (समूह पठन) of four-letter words is recommended to build confidence and correct pronunciation errors in early language learners.
• **Foundation for Advanced Hindi**: Mastering un-matrafied four-letter words lays the indispensable groundwork for successfully learning complex matras (आ, इ, ई, उ, ऊ, etc.) in subsequent chapters.

• **Detailed Word Analysis - 'अदरक' (Ginger)**: 'अ' + 'द' + 'र' + 'क' forms the word 'अदरक', introducing students to a common root vegetable while practicing the sequence of a vowel-starting four-letter combination.
• **Phonetic Breakdown of 'अदरक'**: The word is decoded phonetically as 'A-da-ra-ka', demonstrating how a leading independent vowel combines with three subsequent hard consonants.
• **Visual Context for 'अदरक'**: The textbook pairs the word 'अदरक' with an authentic illustration, helping students link the written lexical symbol to the actual physical object found in domestic kitchens.
• **Fine Motor Tracing for 'अदरक'**: Students practice writing 'अदरक' inside structured double-line writing blocks to master vertical alignment, spacing, and the continuous headline rule of Devanagari script.
• **Detailed Word Analysis - 'अचकन' (Traditional Tunic)**: The word 'अचकन' ('अ' + 'च' + 'क' + 'न') introduces children to a traditional Indian upper garment, expanding their cultural and historical vocabulary.
• **Phonetic Breakdown of 'अचकन'**: Pronounced smoothly as 'A-cha-ka-na', this word helps students practice the palatal voiceless stop 'च' (cha) followed by velar and nasal consonants.
• **Visual Context for 'अचकन'**: An illustration of a graceful traditional coat accompanies the text, giving visual clarity to a word that might otherwise be abstract for a modern kindergartener.
• **Writing Practice - 'अचकन'**: Learners trace and copy 'अचकन' repeatedly to build wrist flexibility and muscle memory required for longer Devanagari character sequences.
• **Detailed Word Analysis - 'बर्तन' (Utensil)**: The word 'बर्तन' ('ब' + 'र' + 'त' + 'न') brings a high-utility household object into the child's reading vocabulary, combining labial, liquid, dental, and nasal sounds.
• **Phonetic Breakdown of 'बर्तन'**: Pronounced as 'Ba-ra-ta-na', the inclusion of the retroflex/dental 'त' and liquid 'र' provides vital tongue-flexibility training for young speakers.
• **Visual Context for 'बर्तन'**: The textbook features clear drawings of metal pots and pans to anchor the meaning of 'बर्तन' in the daily domestic experience of the child.
• **Writing Practice - 'बर्तन'**: Students learn to maintain uniform letter sizing while writing 'बर्तन', ensuring that the letters 'र' and 'त' do not crowd each other.
• **Detailed Word Analysis - 'कसरत' (Exercise)**: The word 'कसरत' ('क' + 'स' + 'र' + 'त') introduces the concept of physical fitness and bodily movement into the early vocabulary curriculum.
• **Phonetic Breakdown of 'कसरत'**: Segmented as 'Ka-sa-ra-ta', this word emphasizes the crisp articulation of the sibilant 'स' (sa) sandwiched between velar and dental consonants.
• **Visual Context for 'कसरत'**: An accompanying picture of a child doing physical exercises helps contextualize the action-oriented noun 'कसरत'.
• **Writing Practice - 'कसरत'**: Learners practice writing 'कसरत' to reinforce the correct formation of the complex sibilant letter 'स' in combination with simpler characters.

• **Detailed Word Analysis - 'शलजम' (Turnip)**: The word 'शलजम' ('श' + 'ल' + 'ज' + 'म') introduces students to the palatal sibilant 'श' (sha) at the very beginning of a four-letter word.
• **Phonetic Breakdown of 'शलजम'**: Pronounced as 'Sha-la-ja-ma', this word trains children in distinguishing the soft sibilant 'श' from the dental sibilant 'स'.
• **Visual Context for 'शलजम'**: A vibrant illustration of a purple-and-white turnip helps children immediately recognize the vegetable and connect it with its Hindi name.
• **Writing Practice - 'शलजम'**: Students carefully trace the intricate top loop and curves of the letter 'श' while writing 'शलजम' within the standard DAV notebook lines.
• **Detailed Word Analysis - 'बरगद' (Banyan Tree)**: The word 'बरगद' ('ब' + 'र' + 'ग' + 'द') introduces children to the national tree of India, blending labial, liquid, velar, and dental consonants.
• **Phonetic Breakdown of 'बरगद'**: Segmented as 'Ba-ra-ga-da', the smooth transition from 'र' to 'ग' builds exceptional oral fluency and breath control in early readers.
• **Visual Context for 'बरगद'**: An expansive drawing of a grand banyan tree with hanging aerial roots provides rich environmental and ecological vocabulary context.
• **Writing Practice - 'बरगद'**: Learners practice the balanced horizontal distribution of characters in 'बरगद', ensuring the hanging loop of 'द' is neatly formed.
• **Detailed Word Analysis - 'अमल्टस' / 'अमरूद' Variant Integration**: The chapter expands further into botanical nouns, teaching children words that represent natural flora encountered in their immediate surroundings.
• **Detailed Word Analysis - 'कटनल' / 'टमटम' (Horse Carriage)**: The word 'टमटम' ('ट' + 'म' + 'ट' + 'म') introduces a classic reduplicated four-letter rhythmic word structure.
• **Phonetic Breakdown of 'टमटम'**: Pronounced as 'Ta-ma-ta-ma', this symmetrical word structure delights young learners with its rhythmic, drum-like phonetic bounce.
• **Visual Context for 'टमटम'**: An illustration of a traditional horse-drawn carriage brings the historical and cultural term 'टमटम' to vivid life for the students.
• **Writing Practice - 'टमटम'**: Students practice writing the retroflex plosive 'ट' alongside the nasal 'म', paying close attention to the unique top-flat cap of 'ट'.
• **Consolidated Word Review (Page 35 of Bal Madhuri)**: The curriculum pauses here to encourage teachers to conduct lightning-round flashcard readings of 'अदरक', 'अचकन', 'बर्तन', and 'कसरत'.
• **Peer Reading Activities**: Children are paired in the classroom to take turns pointing at words and reading them aloud to each other, fostering cooperative learning and social-emotional growth.

• **Detailed Word Analysis - 'नटखट' (Naughty/Mischievous)**: The word 'नटखट' ('न' + 'ट' + 'ख' + 'ट') introduces an adjective describing playful or mischievous behavior common in children.
• **Phonetic Breakdown of 'नटखट'**: Segmented phonetically as 'Na-ta-kha-ta', this word combines nasal, retroflex, aspirated velar, and retroflex sounds in a rapid sequence.
• **Visual Context for 'नटखट'**: An engaging illustration of a playful child helps students grasp the abstract concept of naughtiness through relatable visual storytelling.
• **Writing Practice - 'नटखट'**: Students practice writing 'नटखट', focusing on the distinction between the unaspirated 'ट' and the aspirated 'ख' with its characteristic loop.
• **Detailed Word Analysis - 'झटपट' (Quickly / Fast)**: The word 'झटपट' ('झ' + 'ट' + 'प' + 'ट') introduces an adverb of manner, teaching children how to express speed and prompt action in Hindi.
• **Phonetic Breakdown of 'झटपट'**: Sounded out as 'Jha-ta-pa-ta', this word features the aspirated voiced palatal stop 'झ' combined with retroflex and labial stops.
• **Visual Context for 'झटपट'**: Illustrations depicting quick actions (like running or rushing) help students associate 'झटपट' with the concept of doing things fast.
• **Writing Practice - 'झटपट'**: Learners practice the intricate curves of 'झ' followed by the straight lines of 'ट' and 'प', enhancing fine motor precision.
• **Detailed Word Analysis - 'खटमल' (Bedbug)**: The word 'खटमल' ('ख' + 'ट' + 'म' + 'ल') introduces an insect name, expanding the biological vocabulary of the UKG learner.
• **Phonetic Breakdown of 'खटमल'**: Decoded as 'Kha-ta-ma-la', this word provides excellent practice for combining aspiration ('ख') with nasals ('म') and liquids ('ल').
• **Visual Context for 'खटमल'**: A magnified, child-friendly drawing of the insect helps students identify the creature associated with the word 'खटमल'.
• **Writing Practice - 'खटमल'**: Students execute controlled pen strokes to form 'खटमल', ensuring proper letter spacing and clear separation between each of the four characters.
• **Detailed Word Analysis - 'थरमॉस' / 'दमकल' (Fire Engine)**: The word 'दमकल' ('द' + 'म' + 'क' + 'ल') introduces an emergency service vehicle, teaching civic awareness alongside vocabulary.
• **Phonetic Breakdown of 'दमकल'**: Pronounced as 'Da-ma-ka-la', this word combines dental, nasal, velar, and liquid phonemes into a cohesive public service term.
• **Visual Context for 'दमकल'**: A bright red fire truck illustration accompanies 'दमकल', capturing the immediate attention and imagination of young learners.

• **Detailed Word Analysis - 'बरगद' Comprehensive Review**: A deeper pedagogical look at 'बरगद' reveals how DAV curriculum design embeds environmental respect within basic language lessons.
• **Phonetic Mastery of Liquid Consonants**: The frequent inclusion of 'र' (ra) and 'ल' (la) in words like 'बरगद' and 'शलजम' is purposefully designed to loosen the tongue muscles of children.
• **Syllable Segmentation Drills**: Teachers utilize the two-plus-two segmentation method (e.g., 'बर' + 'गद' = 'बरगद') to teach students how to chunk longer words for easier reading.
• **Sporal Recognition vs. Production**: The chapter ensures that students not only recognize these four-letter words visually but can also reproduce them independently from dictation (श्रुतलेख).
• **Dictation Exercise Framework (श्रुतलेख अभ्यास)**: Structured classroom dictation of words like 'अदरक', 'बर्तन', 'कसरत', and 'झटपट' checks auditory processing and accurate orthographic recall.
• **Error Analysis and Correction**: Common student mistakes—such as omitting the middle letters or reversing 'र' and 'ल'—are systematically addressed through guided chalkboard re-writing.
• **Cross-Curricular Connections**: Vocabulary from Chapter 5 connects language learning with General Science (identifying vegetables like 'शलजम' and trees like 'बरगद').
• **Interactive Word Building Games**: Classrooms utilize physical letter cards where students physically arrange four consonant cards in a straight line to synthesize target vocabulary.
• **Oral Reading Fluency (वाचन प्रवाह)**: Timed or paced reading drills of word lists ensure that students move past halting, letter-by-letter sounding to smooth whole-word recognition.
• **Flashcard Drills Mechanism**: Rapid-fire flashcard presentation of un-matrafied four-letter words builds instantaneous cognitive retrieval speed in five-year-old learners.
• **Home-School Partnership (गृहकार्य निर्देश)**: Parents are instructed via the DAV diary to spend 10 minutes daily having their child read aloud the four-letter word boxes in Bal Madhuri.
• **Reinforcement of Sero-Rekha (सिरोरेखा - Headline)**: Teachers continuously emphasize drawing a single, unbroken horizontal line across all four letters to form a unified Hindi word unit.
• **Avoiding Common Phonetic Traps**: Educators warn students not to inject inherent vowel schwa breaks unnaturally between the third and fourth letters of a four-letter cluster.
• **Multisensory Learning Integration**: Students air-trace four-letter words with their index fingers while chanting the individual phonemes aloud to engage kinesthetic memory.
• **Formative Assessment Checkpoints**: Informal observation checklists are maintained by DAV teachers to track individual student mastery over un-matrafied four-letter combinations.

• **Detailed Word Analysis - 'उपवन' (Garden / Park)**: The word 'उपवन' ('उ' + 'प' + 'व' + 'न') introduces an independent vowel ('उ') combined with three consonants to denote a nature park.
• **Phonetic Breakdown of 'उपवन'**: Segmented as 'U-pa-va-na', this word demonstrates the harmonious blending of an initial vowel with labial and dental consonants.
• **Visual Context for 'उपवन'**: A lush illustration of a garden filled with blooming flowers provides a serene visual anchor for the word 'उपवन'.
• **Writing Practice - 'उपवन'**: Students practice the curved top-open shape of the vowel 'उ' followed by 'प', 'व', and 'न' within standard writing lines.
• **Detailed Word Analysis - 'अचकन' Cultural Enrichment**: Further exploration of 'अचकन' connects students to Indian heritage, festive attire, and cultural celebrations.
• **Detailed Word Analysis - 'मलहम' (Ointment / Balm)**: The word 'मलहम' ('म' + 'ल' + 'ह' + 'म') introduces medical and first-aid vocabulary into the early childhood curriculum.
• **Phonetic Breakdown of 'मलहम'**: Pronounced as 'Ma-la-ha-ma', this word features the breathy glottal fricative 'ह' (ha) embedded between nasal and liquid sounds.
• **Visual Context for 'मलहम'**: An illustration of a medicine tube or healing balm helps children connect the word 'मलहम' with soothing minor scrapes and cuts.
• **Writing Practice - 'मलहम'**: Learners practice writing the complex loop of 'ह' in 'मलहम', mastering its distinct internal curl and downward tail.
• **Detailed Word Analysis - 'करवत' (Saw / Cutting Tool)**: The word 'करवत' ('क' + 'र' + 'व' + 'त') introduces a carpentry tool, expanding the child's awareness of tools used by artisans.
• **Phonetic Breakdown of 'करवत'**: Sounded out as 'Ka-ra-va-ta', this word exercises the flexible transition from velar stops to liquids, labiodentals, and dental stops.
• **Visual Context for 'करवत'**: A clear drawing of a hand-saw provides immediate visual comprehension of the instrument named 'करवत'.
• **Writing Practice - 'करवत'**: Students trace and write 'करवत', ensuring the semi-circular curve of 'व' is properly formed without confusion with 'ब'.
• **Detailed Word Analysis - 'उपहार' / 'अक्षर' Integration**: Expanding on letter combinations, students review how multiple consonants can form stable, pronounceable four-letter blocks.
• **Rhythmic Chanting Exercises**: Teachers lead the class in rhythmic chanting of four-letter words in a musical cadence to make vocabulary acquisition joyful and memorable.

• **Sentence Formation Bridge (शब्दों से वाक्य निर्माण)**: Chapter 5 transitions students from isolated four-letter words to reading simple, connected sentences containing these words.
• **Reading Simple Sentences (सरल वाक्यों का पठन)**: Students encounter sentences like "अदरक चख" (Taste ginger) and "कसरत कर" (Do exercise), applying their four-letter word knowledge in context.
• **Integration with Two and Three-Letter Words**: Sentences in this section cleverly mix two-letter, three-letter, and four-letter words to create realistic, flowing Hindi syntax.
• **Understanding Punctuation (पूर्ण विराम)**: Children are introduced to the Hindi full stop symbol ('।' - *Purna Viram*) at the end of each practice sentence.
• **Phonetic Reading of Sentences**: Teachers guide children to sweep their fingers smoothly under entire sentences rather than stopping rigidly after every single word.
• **Sentence Drill - "अमन, अचकन पहन"**: Students read and comprehend the command-based sentence instructing Aman to wear his traditional tunic.
• **Sentence Drill - "नटखट मत बन"**: Children learn moral and behavioral instruction through language practice, reading "Do not be mischievous."
• **Sentence Drill - "झटपट बर्तन रख"**: A practical instruction sentence ("Keep the utensils quickly") combining multiple four-letter words into a unified command.
• **Sentence Drill - "शलजम चख कर रख"**: A multi-word sentence linking tasting action with placing the vegetable down, building advanced reading stamina.
• **Comprehension Check Mechanism**: Teachers ask basic oral questions about the sentences read (e.g., "Who should wear the achkan?") to ensure cognitive understanding alongside decoding.
• **Reading Fluency Standards for UKG**: By the end of this chapter's sentence section, DAV students are expected to read simple 4-to-5-word sentences without stuttering.
• **Chalkboard Modeling by Teachers**: Educators demonstrate proper eye-tracking across sentences on the classroom blackboard, modeling left-to-right reading discipline.
• **Peer Reading Circles**: Students sit in small circles, taking turns reading one sentence each from the Bal Madhuri reader to build public speaking confidence.
• **Individual Reading Evaluations**: Teachers conduct one-on-one reading assessments where each child reads a designated paragraph of four-letter words and sentences aloud.
• **Positive Reinforcement Practices**: Stellar reading performance is rewarded with star stamps or verbal praise, reinforcing intrinsic motivation for Hindi literacy.

• **Comprehensive Vocabulary Compilation**: A master list of all four-letter words introduced in Chapter 5 is compiled for holistic review and examination preparation.
• **Category-wise Word Sorting**: Words are organized into thematic categories by teachers—Vegetables (अदरक, शलजम), Objects (बर्तन, टमटम), Actions (कसरत, झटपट), and Traits (नटखट).
• **Memory Retention Strategies**: Teachers employ mnemonic devices and rhyming association games to help students remember spellings of challenging four-letter combinations.
• **Visual Flashcard Matching Games**: Classroom activities involve matching word flashcards ('मलहम', 'बरगद', 'उपवन') to their respective pictorial representations on a display board.
• **Fill-in-the-Blank Precursors**: Simple missing-letter exercises (e.g., अ_रक -> अदरक) are introduced orally to test orthographic memory without overwhelming the young learner.
• **Correct Pronunciation (शुद्ध उच्चारण) Focus**: Special attention is paid to eradicating regional mother-tongue influences on the pronunciation of sounds like 'ष', 'श', and 'स'.
• **Breath Control in Longer Words**: Students are taught how to sustain breath evenly across four continuous syllables without gasping or breaking word unity.
• **Writing Posture and Grip Correction**: Teachers monitor pencil grip (tripod grasp) and notebook tilt during the extensive writing practice sessions required for Chapter 5.
• **Neatness and Cleanliness Standards**: Strict adherence to erasures without tearing paper and keeping margins clean is instilled as a core DAV notebook discipline.
• **Homework Assignment Structure**: Home tasks involve tracing words three times in the homework notebook and reading aloud to a family member daily.
• **Parental Feedback Integration**: Parents sign off in the student diary confirming that home reading practice was successfully completed.
• **Remodial Teaching Strategies**: Students struggling with four-letter blending receive extra, specialized small-group instruction focusing on two-plus-two syllable chunking.
• **Advanced Learner Enrichment**: Faster learners are encouraged to think of additional un-matrafied four-letter words not explicitly printed in the textbook.
• **Cultural Value Integration**: Lessons on respect for nature ('उपवन', 'बरगद') and physical discipline ('कसरत') are woven into daily value-education moments.
• **Transition Readiness Assessment**: The completion of Chapter 5 officially certifies that the UKG student is ready to advance toward matra-based learning.

• **Teacher's Instructional Methodology Guidelines**: Educators are advised to use multisensory approaches—visuals, auditory sounding, tactile writing, and kinesthetic movement.
• **Phonemic Awareness Milestones**: By completing this chapter, students achieve complete phonemic awareness of non-compound Devanagari consonant clusters.
• **Curriculum Alignment with NEP 2020**: Chapter 5 aligns with National Education Policy guidelines by prioritizing experiential learning, foundational literacy, and conceptual clarity.
• **Development of Cognitive Agility**: Processing four distinct symbols in immediate succession exercises working memory and cognitive sequencing in early childhood.
• **Self-Correction Capabilities**: Students learn to inspect their written words against the textbook model, spotting and correcting misplaced loops or broken headlines.
• **Vocabulary Expansion Impact**: The addition of dozens of new four-letter nouns, adjectives, and verbs significantly boosts the child's active and passive Hindi vocabulary.
• **Classroom Display Boards (Bal Vatika Display)**: Student artwork and neat handwriting samples of four-letter words are pinned on classroom display boards for peer appreciation.
• **Interactive Storytelling Extensions**: Teachers invent short, engaging moral stories incorporating target words like 'नटखट बालक' and 'हरा भरा उपवन' to contextualize learning.
• **Oral Expression and Vocabulary Usage**: Students are encouraged to use newly learned words in spoken sentences during free-play conversation circles.
• **Addressing Common Orthographic Confusions**: Special drills are conducted to prevent confusion between visually similar letters like 'ब' and 'व', or 'न' and 'म'.
• **Building Stamina for Long-Form Writing**: Chapter 5 serves as the vital stepping stone that builds the hand stamina needed for multi-word dictation in Class 1.
• **Holistic Assessment Overview**: Evaluation encompasses oral reading fluency, dictation accuracy, visual identification, and neatness in written execution.
• **Celebration of Learning Milestones**: The successful conclusion of Chapter 5 is marked by a celebratory classroom reading session where every child reads aloud a favorite word.
• **Seamless Progression to Chapter 6**: The chapter concludes by setting the stage for subsequent DAV modules that introduce dependent vowel signs (मात्राएँ).
• **Final Academic Summary**: Chapter 5 ("चार अक्षर वाले शब्दों का अभ्यास") stands as a masterclass in foundational phonetic literacy, successfully bridging simple phonemes to complex word structures.

• **Master Glossary of Chapter 5 Vocabulary**: 
  - अदरक (Adarak) - Ginger
  - अचकन (Achkan) - Traditional Tunic
  - बर्तन (Bartan) - Utensil
  - कसरत (Kasrat) - Exercise
  - शलजम (Shaljam) - Turnip
• **Master Glossary (Continued - Part 2)**:
  - बरगद (Bargad) - Banyan Tree
  - टमटम (Tamtam) - Horse Carriage
  - नटखट (Natkhat) - Naughty
  - झटपट (Jhatpat) - Quickly
  - खटमल (Khatmal) - Bedbug
• **Master Glossary (Continued - Part 3)**:
  - दमकल (Damkal) - Fire Engine
  - उपवन (Upvan) - Garden / Park
  - मलहम (Malham) - Ointment / Balm
  - करवत (Karvat) - Saw / Cutting Tool
• **Key Pedagogical Takeaways for Educators**: Consistent daily practice of breaking four-letter words into two-letter phonetic chunks guarantees long-term reading success.
• **Key Takeaways for Students**: Reading without matras requires patience, careful eye-tracking from left to right, and precise blending of individual consonant sounds.
• **Role of Visual Aids in Retention**: Pictures are not mere decorations but essential cognitive hooks that anchor abstract linguistic symbols into concrete real-world meanings.
• **Importance of the Sero-Rekha**: Maintaining a continuous horizontal line over all four letters is non-negotiable for proper Devanagari script formation and aesthetic neatness.
• **Final DAV Board Quality Assurance Statement**: These comprehensive study notes have been meticulously curated in accordance with the Dayanand Anglo-Vedic Public School Board academic framework for Class UKG Bal Madhuri.
